name: The Cradle Drop (Viral Sensory Deprivation Trend)
description: A viral practice that swept M88 between 2222 and 2224 in which participants use BCI suppression patches — originally developed for medical sensory overload treatment — to voluntarily blank all external sensory input for exactly ninety seconds in a public space, typically a crowded transit hub or market, remaining physically present but perceptually absent. Practitioners describe the experience as 'returning to before you were anything,' and the trend's name derives from the posture participants naturally adopt: a slight forward curl, arms loose, called the cradle position by early adopters. The trend was documented first among Tier 2 transit workers but spread rapidly to Tier 4 professionals, and a secondary culture of 'Watchers' has emerged — people who do not participate but attend to observe and document.
cultural_impact: The Cradle Drop prompted the first serious public debate about BCI suppression patch regulation, with three corponations filing legislative proposals to restrict patch availability — framing recreational use as a public safety hazard — while medical advocacy groups argued the debate was cover for restricting legitimate therapeutic access.
key_figures: Nneka Petrov-Hashimoto (Tier 2 transit worker credited as first documented participant)
Dr. Soren Abubakar-Lindh (neurologist who popularized the medical framing)
locations: The Cradle Corner — an informal designated zone in Meridian Central Market
story_hooks: A Cradle Drop participant doesn't come back — body present, BCI patch expired, but the person remains in the cradle position, unresponsive, for going on six hours and counting.
Someone has been modifying BCI suppression patches sold at a specific Shelf vendor to extend the blackout period far beyond ninety seconds, and three people have gone missing after extended drops.
The Watcher Collective has compiled footage suggesting that during Cradle Drops, participants' bodies sometimes move — slightly, purposefully — in ways the participants themselves have no memory of.
